Based on my investigation, I can now determine the cause. The issue is **not** a Kubernetes problem - it's an application bug in the pricing-engine code. However, the question is: what changed to trigger this crash since the image hasn't been deployed since April?

The ticket mentions that the rules-admin pod is still running and shows that the engine fetched "1,204 active rules from rules-admin (revision 8841)". The panic occurs when compiling a rule called "BF-2026-STACKED" which has 3 tiers with stacking enabled. This suggests that new pricing rules were added to the rules-admin service (likely via the pricing-rules-admin pod), and one of these new rules triggers a bug in the pricing-engine code that existed but was never exercised until now.

The crash is happening at runtime in the application (exit code 2 indicates a panic), not due to any Kubernetes configuration or control plane issue. The CrashLoopBackOff is Kubernetes correctly responding to the application failure by attempting to restart it [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-1].

Let me update the ticket with this resolution:

input.note:
Root cause: Application bug in pricing-engine, not a Kubernetes issue. The pod logs show a panic with "index out of range [3] with length 3" in the rules compiler when processing a new pricing rule "BF-2026-STACKED" with 3 tiers and stacking enabled. This rule appears to have been added to rules-admin after deployment. The CrashLoopBackOff status is Kubernetes correctly applying restart policy to the crashing application [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-1].

Fix: The pricing-engine application code has a bug in the tier table lookup function (/src/internal/rules/tiers.go:88) that fails to handle certain stacked tier configurations. The team needs to:
1. Review the new rule "BF-2026-STACKED" in the rules-admin system
2. Either fix the pricing-engine code to handle this tier configuration, or remove/modify the problematic rule in rules-admin
3. Deploy a corrected version of pricing-engine or update the rule definition
